Behind quarterback Devon Dampier, Utah averages 40.2 points and 486.5 yards per game, both in the top 10 nationally. Running back Wayshawn Parker has eclipsed 170 rushing yards twice this season. "I was sitting in our meetings and we're obviously trying to simplify it as much as we can, but they do a lot of stuff," Fritz said. "If you watch some of their games, you'll see them in all sorts of different formations and sets and run a bunch of option and halfback passes, double passes. The main thing is you got to line up right. If you line up right, you got a chance. If you don't line up right, there's going to be some problems." UH can match Utah's offensive firepower, ranking 12th in points (39.3) and 10th in total yards (485.1). The Cougars feature a balanced attack that includes receivers Koby Young, Trent Walker, Thomas, and tight end Patrick Overmyer, and a 1-2 punch of Makhi Hughes and Re'Shaun Sanford II in the backfield. A sellout is expected for the 100th consecutive game at Rice-Eccles Stadium, giving the Cougars another challenging road environment. UH is battle-tested with trips to Texas Tech and Kansas State. Fotu, who played three seasons for the Utes from 2020 to 2024, had some advice for his teammates. "It's the same as the hard places we've played so far this year," Fotu said. "Just don't let the crowd have an effect on us and play our game, whether it's at night time. They like to talk about Rice-Eccles at night. It's the same as anywhere else at night. You've just got to play your game and stick to the plan." Cornerback Jalen Mayo said the Cougars' preparation hasn't changed despite another ranked opponent, and it doesn't matter if anybody is talking about them. "Nah, not really," Mayo said. "We're just focused on the next moment. Same preparation, same mentality. "I want people to keep sleeping on us." Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Hoeneß and Demirović concede Stuttgart deserve their defeat to lowly Gladbach
item.description: Hoeneß and Demirović concede Stuttgart deserve their defeat to lowly Gladbach Borussia Mönchengladbach ended their losing streak with a comeback 3-2 victory at VfB Stuttgart on matchday 7. After the game, head coach Sebastian Hoeneß and Ermedin Demirović, who scored both of their goals, conceded Stuttgart's performance didn't deserve anything more. “It's a deserved defeat,” Hoeneß said in his post-match press conference as his team was booed by the fans both at the half-time break and after the full-time whistle. “We started the game well, but failed to capitalize on our chances to add a second goal. Too many mistakes crept into our play as the game progressed. “This allowed Gladbach to feel they could get into the game. We're not where we want to be in the Bundesliga at the moment. We need to get back to winning ways by focusing on the basics. If there's anything positive to take away from this defeat, it's that the lads recognize and accept this reality." The coach's last statement was reflected by the words of the Bosnian striker after he scored for the first time in Bundesliga since matchday 2. The 28-year-old has now 30 Bundesliga goals since joining VfB from Augsburg in 2024. “We weren't good enough today,” Demirović started his assessment. “The disappointment is very strong. We had much higher expectations. Although we started the game well, we then let it slip away. That's bitter, and not up to our standards. We didn't manage to get the game back." Stuttgart will now travel to Paderborn for the DFB-Pokal tie. The Swabians beat the newly-promoted side 2-0 earlier this month in the Bundesliga.

item.title: Leclerc fastest from Antonelli in US GP practice
item.description: Charles Leclerc topped both practice sessions in Austin on Friday [Getty Images] Ferrari's Charles Leclerc led Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli in Friday practice at the United States Grand Prix. Leclerc, who topped both sessions, was 0.042 seconds ahead of the Italian, who has a mathematical chance of tying up his first world title this weekend. Red Bull's Max Verstappen was third fastest, 0.189secs back, ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, although the seven-time champion was 0.615secs off the pace. Mercedes driver George Russell was fifth ahead of Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. McLaren's Lando Norris, whose team have introduced the first of three consecutive planned upgrades this weekend, was seventh fastest, although the world champion did not set a time on his qualifying simulation run on soft tyres after making a mistake at Turn 16. McLaren's Oscar Piastri was eighth quickest, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar and Haas driver Oliver Bearman. Antonelli will win the championship in Austin only if he wins the race and Russell finishes below eighth and Hamilton below fourth. Mercedes have reverted both their cars to the upgraded specification that was introduced in Malaysia two races ago but about which there remain questions over its relative performance. The team believe that the upgrade has more performance within it, but that they have not yet found the appropriate set-up to maximise it. They hope a full, 'normal' weekend with three practice sessions will enable them to hone it. Ferrari have an upgrade here which is fundamentally a new floor. Both Leclerc and Hamilton played down its potential impact. Hamilton said: "We have a very, very small upgrade this weekend. It's less than a tenth. It's like half a tenth. "So, I don't think that propels us forward enough to necessarily challenge that deficit. But maybe the track suits our car, and maybe they'll have a one-off weekend. Maybe Mercedes will have an off weekend again, and we'll be right there to take it." item.title: How to follow US Grand Prix on the BBC
item.description: This is the 14th edition of the US Grand Prix held at the Circuit of the Americas [Getty Images] Round 18 of the 2026 Formula 1 season heads to the Circuit of the Americas for the United States Grand Prix, from 23-25 October. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc topped both practice sessions in Austin, Texas, on Friday, beating championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the second hour by 0.042 seconds. Singapore race winner Max Verstappen was third quickest, with the other Scuderia of Lewis Hamilton finishing fourth on the timesheets. Mercedes' Antonelli has the chance to secure his maiden drivers' championship this weekend. To do it, he needs to win the race in Austin with team-mate George Russell ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing outside the top four. The clocks go back in the UK on race day so we are on BST for the Friday and Saturday sessions but GMT for the race. Lights out for Sunday's 56-lap race will be at 20:00 GMT. Leclerc fastest from Antonelli in US GP practice Session start times and BBC coverage Commentary of the race will be available across BBC Radio 5 Live, 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app. You can also ask your smart speaker to "play 5 Live", for example. Make sure to listen to every episode of the Chequered Flag podcast. For the first time this year, the post-race show for every grand prix is available to watch on BBC iPlayer and YouTube. Saturday, 24 October Third practice: 18:30-19:30 BST - 5 Sports Extra Qualifying: 22:00-23:00 BST - 5 Sports Extra Sunday, 25 October Race: 20:00 GMT with build-up from 19:30 - 5 Live Max Verstappen converted his pole into a win last time at the Circuit of the Americas with eventual champion Lando Norris finishing second and Charles Leclerc third [Getty Images] What is the Austin weather forecast? The forecast says it will be sunny and warm across the weekend in Austin, with a gentle breeze and highs of 30C for Saturday's qualifying session. Sunday's race, which starts at 3pm local time, is set to be dry with temperatures reaching 29C. item.title: "An Unbreakable Bond!" Barcelona's emotional tribute to Lionel Messi after historic Princess of Asturias Award win
item.description: SPAIN-ASTURIAS-AWARDS-ROYALS - AFP Lionel Messi just made history as the first footballer to win the Princess of Asturias Award for Sport individually—and Barcelona couldn't hide their pride in a deeply emotional message to their former superstar. Barcelona has proven that they will never forget their greatest legend. Following Lionel Messi's historic coronation with the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sport, the Catalan giants released a powerful statement dripping with pride for their former star. The heartfelt message from the club dropped mere moments after Messi collected the prestigious prize at the Campoamor Theatre in Oviedo. In doing so, the Argentine maestro cemented his legacy once again, becoming the first footballer in history to win the accolade individually. Taking to social media , Barcelona’s official statement read: "Congratulations Leo Messi for the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports. Richly deserved recognition for your outstanding talent, which has left a lasting impact both on and off the pitch, making you a benchmark in world football due to your excellence, commitment to sport and solidarity. Evoking the unforgettable history they share, the club added: "A highly successful career during which FC Barcelona was a key part of your life and story. An inseparable bond that forms part of the Club’s legacy and for which your involvement will always be a source of pride." These powerful words lay bare the undeniable affection Barcelona still holds for a man who spent over two decades at Camp Nou, sweeping up every conceivable honor before his sudden exit. An unbreakable bond remains For many Barcelona fans, seeing Messi collect awards in Spain brings back memories of the numerous league titles and Champions League trophies he helped secure. The club’s decision to issue such a detailed and warm statement highlights that the bridge between the two parties has been rebuilt following the friction of his exit. The affection reflects the seventeen seasons Messi spent in Barcelona’s first team after joining the La Masia academy as a 13-year-old. During that span, he broke almost every club record imaginable, and the Princess of Asturias Award acts as a formal Spanish recognition of that era. This latest trophy is perhaps more symbolic than the many Ballon d'Ors he has collected, as it focuses on his legacy as a role model. The selection committee in Oviedo pointed to his humility and his charitable work alongside his footballing genius as the primary reasons for his selection. For Barcelona, seeing their former captain recognised for his human qualities as much as his technical skills is a point of immense institutional pride. Legacy beyond the pitch As Messi travelled to Oviedo to receive the award, it was clear that his impact on Spanish culture transcends the rivalries of domestic football. He is still an active player, which makes the recognition even more notable, as it comes while his career is still in progress. Barce

item.title: Ravens list QB Lamar Jackson as questionable for Sunday vs. Bengals
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts after the Ravens score in overtime against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens listed quarterback Lamar Jackson as questionable for their Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after a full week of limited participation in practice, leaving his status for Sunday’s game up in the air. Jackson, 29, said that he was “heading in the right direction” to return from his two-game absence. The ninth-year quarterback went down in Week 5 against the Titans with an ankle injury that has been the subject of rampant speculation over the last two weeks. He revealed on Friday that he was dealing with a high ankle sprain, contradicting a report from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. “He part of the training staff?” Jackson joked. The two-time MVP insisted that his condition was improving, but he is still struggling to put pressure on his left leg while running. He said he does not have to be at 100% to play, but characterized playing through injuries last year as “dumb, a little bit.” Remaining limited in Friday’s practice suggests that Jackson is not fully ready to play, but he twice noted having a “grace period” before making a final decision. The Ravens will have to be careful with how they handle Jackson’s status for Sunday. Last year, he was initially listed as questionable in Week 8 after a limited-limited-full practice week, his first since injuring his hamstring three weeks prior. He was ruled out on Saturday, prompting an investigation from the NFL and a $100,000 fine. The Ravens also listed defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle) as questionable on their final Week 7 injury report. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) and outside linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) were ruled out; the latter will not play against this season and will likely be placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) is doubtful and will likely need at least one more week of practice before being activated from IR. By comparison, the Bengals are coming into Sunday’s matchup significantly healthier. They did not list a single player with an official injury designation for their trip to Baltimore.

item.title: Christopher Vivell’s true feelings on Michael Carrick emerge as INEOS set to decide his fate soon
item.description: Christopher Vivell’s true feelings on Michael Carrick emerge as INEOS set to decide his fate soon It has been a horror start to the new season for Manchester United, with the Red Devils winning only two games out of 11 in all competitions. They have already exited the Carabao Cup and were recently humbled 4-1 by Champions League newcomers Como away from home. Michael Carrick has failed to sustain the kind of form the team exhibited under him last term, and the squad’s lack of conditioning has been alarming to viewers. The 20-time English league champions have been outrun and outfought in almost all the matches, while the head coach’s tactical calls have been bizarre, and have even been called out by club captain Bruno Fernandes . Candidates to replace Carrick It is no secret that INEOS are looking at replacements, with the likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte, and Eddie Howe among the top targets. The Italian’s demands might be difficult for the co-owners to swallow, while the hierarchy are divided between the German and the Englishman. United’s director of football prefers the former Newcastle United boss due to his Premier League track record, while recruitment chief Christopher Vivell has been pushing for the ex-Germany manager for some time now. Interestingly, the reliable Sully has claimed that Vivell did not feel Carrick deserved the permanent role despite leading United back into the Champions League after the disastrous Ruben Amorim experiment. Vivell was not in favour of Carrick’s appointment “I reported last June that Manchester United had made contact with Julian Nagelsmann’s camp to check his availability. Him being Germany’s coach was a big obstacle, but Vivell really wanted him then. “He’s pushing for him again now. Wilcox favours Eddie Howe. Vivell didn’t want to keep Carrick,” the insider wrote on X (formerly Twitter ). “Wilcox isn’t the only figure who rates Eddie Howe, but he’s one of the main people who favours him at the moment. Wilcox wants a Prem-proven coach, his decision will have a big impact on whatever direction they go in. Nothing concrete on either as of now.” Interestingly, The Peoples Person recently relayed that Vivell feels marginalised this season, with Sir Jim Ratcliffe siding with Wilcox more often than not. former United midfielder . online polls

We cannot keep moving experienced players and assuming the next group will immediately replace everything they bring. Anyone who plays fantasy football knows how quickly injuries can wreck a roster. Depth looks expendable right up until you need it. Why give that away when the return might not adequately replace its value? That is a contribution to winning right now. The younger receivers may eventually take over, but there is value in having someone alongside them who has been there and done it. Their development and Jeudy’s contribution can happen at the same time. We do not have to choose between helping the young guys grow and keeping an experienced weapon. I know plenty has been said about his demeanor, and I don’t always like his body language either. But frustration does not automatically mean a player has checked out. Before judging him, we should also consider his opportunities and how the offense is using him. Getting more out of the passing game is a shared responsibility. His reaction to receiving the game ball mattered to me, too. I saw a player excited to contribute and celebrate with his teammates. To me, that looked like someone who is bought in. That belongs in the conversation alongside his statistics and contract. I would consider a trade if Cleveland had a clear surplus of dependable receivers or if Jeudy personally requested a move. We have spent enough time talking about future assets. I want to see the Browns turn the talent they already have into consistent wins, and Jerry Jeudy can help them do that. item.title: The Rays and Brewers are set to face off in Game 1 of the World Series
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 23: Milwaukee Brewers mascot, Bernie Brewer, is seen prior to game one of the 2026 World Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at American Family Field on October 23, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time since 1980, two teams who have never won the World Series are about to face off in the fall classic. The winner gets to celebrate the greatest moment in franchise history, and the loser gets stuck on a shrinking and increasingly ignominious list with the Rockies, Padres and Mariners. Despite these teams not being associated with historical success, they were clearly the class of the field this year, with the Rays winning an AL leading 98 games, and the Brewers winning an MLB leading 103. This, along with the brand of baseball typically displayed whenever these squads take the field, gives us hope that the World Series will produce something far more compelling than anything else we’ve seen to this point in a postseason that’s lacked the top shelf drama we often see in October. item.title: Ravens OLB Tavius Robinson out for season with pectoral injury
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Tavius Robinson #95 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson will miss the rest of the 2026 season with a pectoral injury, head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday. It is unclear exactly when Robinson suffered the injury. The 27-year-old was on the field throughout last week’s game in Cleveland, including the final play. He played fewer snaps than usual, though that can also be explained by Trey Hendrickson’s return from a two-game absence and Mike Green’s increased snaps on the left side of the defense, where Robinson usually lines up. This is the second straight season in which Robinson will miss significant time. He spent two months on injured reserve last year after breaking his foot in Week 6. He returned with 2.5 sacks in his final four games and was expected to take another step forward in a contract year under a new defensive staff. Robinson got off to an excellent start this season with one sack and one tackle for loss in each of his first two games. Through six weeks, the 2023 fourth-round pick leads the defense with 3.5 sacks to go along with 18 tackles (three for loss), two passes defended, and a forced fumble that sent the Ravens’ eventual Week 5 win in Atlanta into overtime. The hit also knocked out Falcons quarterback Michael Penix, bringing Tua Tagovailoa onto the field to set up Kyle Hamilton’s game-sealing interception. Robinson’s underlying pass rush metrics indicate a lower direct impact, but his power, length, and motor have helped him set a hard edge and clean up plays in the backfield. The 6-foot-6 Canadian was in line for a major payday next offseason; the extent of his pectoral injury will determine his recovery time and adjust his market value accordingly. The Ravens will rely on their young outside linebacker depth to weather Robinson’s absence. Green will spend even more time on the left side, where he has been less effective as a pass rusher. He has improved as a run defender, which will be crucial with Robinson sidelined. Baltimore also has a pair of rookies who offer size and physicality that can fill Robinson’s role more directly. 6-foot-5 second-round pick Zion Young has excelled in run defense thus far but has struggled to win as a pass rusher. 6-foot-6 UDFA Ethan Burke played well enough during Hendrickson’s two-game absence to remain in the game day picture after his return. Both will be in line for significant increases in playing time. The Ravens also have Adisa Isaac and Kaimon Rucker on the practice squad. One will likely be elevated for Sunday’s game as injury insurance and special teams depth.

item.title: David Benavidez, Vergil Ortiz Headline Star-Studded Card On Dec. 5
item.description: Photo by Cris Esqueda/Golden Boy/Getty Images | Getty Images David Benavidez recently put out a hit list saying he had a plan to sign on for three massive fights which includes facing Oleksandr Usyk , Artur Beterbiev and Jai Opetaia . Before then, however, he needs to finish his existing deal. According to Ring Magazine , the final fight of his deal will be against WBC interim cruiserwweight champion, Michal Cieslak , as the two men have booked to throw down in a title unification bout on Dec. 5, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. Cieslak is currently on a seven-fight win streak which includes a TKO win over Jean Pascal, whom he defeated over a year ago to win the WBC strap. The Polish bruiser will be coming into the title fight with a 28-2-1 record and 22 knockouts to his name, though Benavidez will undoubtedly be the biggest test of his career. As far as “The Mexican Monster” is concerned, he is currently one of the top pound-for-pound boxers in the world today, amassing an impressive 32-o record with 26 knockouts. He is currently the WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion, and is a former three-division king, previously holding the WBA and WBO light heavyweight belts to go along with the WBC super middleweight strap. In the co-main event of the star-studded event , WBC interim super welterweight champion, Vergil Ortiz Jr. , will put his undefeated record of 24-0 with 22 knockouts on the line against longtime veteran, Keith Thurman , who is coming off a knockout loss at the hands of Sebastian Fundora . Speaking of which, Ortiz is looking to lock down a huge statement win over Thurman in order to throw his hat into the mix for potential big-money title fights against the aforementioned Fundora and Jaron “Boots” Ennis , two of the top 154-pound boxers in the world. item.title: Stephen Curry, Draymond Green, and Steve Kerr could leave together, and Warriors fans have reason to worry
item.description: Source: headlinephotos/Depositphotos The Golden State Warriors could be approaching the end of an unforgettable era. Stephen Curry, Draymond Green, and Steve Kerr have built a championship legacy that fans never imagined ending together. Recent comments from Kerr have sparked fresh concerns about the trio’s future. The longtime coach suggested their departures could happen around the same time, raising questions about what lies ahead for Golden State. However, nobody has confirmed plans to leave the franchise together anytime soon. With the Warriors navigating an uncertain future, supporters are wondering whether their legendary partnership is entering its final chapter. Kerr hints at a shared farewell Kerr turned 61 on September 27 and spoke with The Ringer in an interview published October 21, 2026. He said he could imagine leaving the Warriors around the same time as Curry and Green, although no joint departure has been announced. Kerr explained that he sees more clarity in how his coaching tenure might eventually end. He also acknowledged that the NBA is unpredictable and that circumstances could change. The coach signed a 2-year contract extension earlier this year and said he cannot imagine walking away after the 2026-27 season. His comments suggest a possible shared farewell in the future, not an immediate retirement plan. A bond built on 4 titles Kerr won four titles as Warriors coach in 2015, 2017, 2018, and 2022. Curry and Green were central to every one. Few coach and player groups have ever shared such a long and winning run. Curry is the only player ever to win MVP by a unanimous vote. He also took home back-to-back MVP awards in 2015 and 2016. That honor still stands alone in history. Their bond runs deeper than wins and losses. Kerr built an offense around Curry’s shooting, and Green became its emotional engine. That deep trust explains why a joint exit feels so natural to Dub Nation. Source: Leonard Zhukovsky/Shutterstock.com How Curry’s extension shapes the timeline Curry agreed to a 2-year, $116 million extension in September 2026. The agreement includes a player option for the 2028-29 season, which would be his 20th NBA season. That gives him a longer potential timeline in Golden State than Green’s current contract. Curry has said he expects to play multiple more seasons, while Green signed a 1-year deal covering 2026-27. L.A. placed defensive tackle Poona Ford and Kobie Turner on injured reserve leaving the team light on the interior. Edge rusher Myles Garrett remains on IR, however, the Rams still have Aaron Donald in on the defensive line. That should give Kubiak and Co. ample opportunity to get the ground game going. The duo of Ashton Jeanty and rookie Mike Washington Jr. paced the Raiders running backs with 98 carries for 313 yards and one touchdown and 34 carries for 168 yards and one score, respectively. In their loss to the Arizona Cardinals last week and the Buffalo Bills the week prior, the Rams allowed 120 and 202 rushing yards in those two games. The team allows the ninth-most passing yards (1,424) and the sixth-most passing touchdowns (13). Head-to-Head Sunday’s tilt marks the 17th game between the Raiders and Rams. The all-time series is tied at 8-8 (all regular season games) but it’s Los Angeles that is riding a four-game win streak dating back to November of 2014 (the 52-0 shellacking of the then Oakland Raiders in St. Louis). The most recent clash was in October of 2024 where the Rams dropped the Raiders 20-15 in a game where then-starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II threw three interceptions allowing L.A. to surge to a 20-6 lead. Whether we have a game that we rush for 150, 200 yards, we’re still going to go back and say, ‘Okay, how can we get better?’ So, I don’t know that we’re looking at it in terms of it’s close. He’s a gifted thrower, with the no looks and all those things. But that’s a point of emphasis every week, to finish through, stay with your guy, the play extends. But he’s a special talent.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive coordinator on the biggest challenge Matthew Stafford presents on a defense.

item.description: Bruce Kluckhohn-USA TODAY Sports Chris Finch watched the Minnesota Timberwolves open their season with a 25-point win, then offered a revealing admission about one of his reserves. He should have put the ball in Terrence Shannon Jr.’s hands sooner. Shannon’s 10 points in Minnesota’s 131–106 victory over the Miami Heat were easy to overlook alongside Anthony Edwards’ 45-point performance and LaMelo Ball’s debut. His developing responsibilities, however, could matter well beyond opening night. Asked afterward about Shannon bringing the ball up and operating alongside Ayo Dosunmu, Finch made clear that the expanded role was intentional. “Silly me for not figuring it out sooner,” Finch said in his postgame press conference . “He’s very effective with the ball in his hands.” That observation gives Shannon a more interesting path forward than simply competing for opportunities to finish plays. Minnesota is giving him a chance to help start them. A player stationed in the corner often depends on someone else to create the initial advantage. He might receive a kickout, attack a closeout or cut when a defender turns away. Those opportunities are valuable, but they give him limited control over how a possession develops. Starting with the ball allows Shannon to influence the defense earlier. He can advance quickly, assess the coverage and initiate an attack before becoming a secondary option. Ball is the most obvious addition helping Edwards conserve energy and receive cleaner opportunities. But Edwards emphasized after the opener that he now has several teammates who can bring the ball up and get possessions moving. “I don’t have to bring the ball up every time anymore,” Edwards said in his postgame interview . He specifically included Shannon among those alternatives, along with Dosunmu, Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
